thread.title: ICE Facility Accused of Breaking Detention Limits - NewsBreak
thread.title_full: ICE Facility Accused of Breaking Detention Limits - NewsBreak

author: Sarah Bennett
title: ICE Facility Accused of Breaking Detention Limits - NewsBreak
text:
By Sarah Bennett ,
53 minutes ago Portland City officials have planned a land-use violation notice for an Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) facility after it allegedly held individuals beyond the 12-hour limit. Critics raised concerns about prolonged detentions, prompting the city to formally review ICE’s compliance. A separate citation addresses boarded windows, unrelated to land-use approval.
Under city rules, the operator has 30 days to address issues after a notice. A reconsideration hearing can occur at least 60 days after the notice.
A Deportation Data Project report found 25 instances from October to July of people held beyond the limit. Mayor Keith Wilson said the facility repeatedly broke its detention-duration commitments.
Wilson stated, “U.S. Immigrations and Customs Enforcement made clear detention limitation commitments to our community, and we believe they broke those policies more than two dozen times.”
Wilson added, “I am proud of our team for conducting a thorough, thoughtful investigation and referring the matter to the next steps in the land use violation process.”
The building, leased and managed by the General Services Administration, houses a processing center for detaining and interviewing individuals on immigration status. It has remained a protest focal point, with some demonstrations turning violent.
DHS Assistant Secretary Tricia McLaughlin said, “Another day, another sanctuary politician attempting to prevent the brave men and women of ICE from removing the worst of the worst, including rapists, murderers, pedophiles, and gang members from the U.S. Mayor Wilson’s claims of substandard conditions at ICE facilities are categorically FALSE. All detainees receive proper meals, medical care, and access to family and legal counsel.”
McLaughlin added, “Furthermore, the southwest Portland ICE facility is a processing center, not a detention center. Detainees are briefly processed before being transferred to detention facilities.”
Portland’s sanctuary policies prevent city employees, including police, from enforcing federal immigration law. Oregon law bars state and local involvement in immigration enforcement without a warrant.
Wilson said, “You can rest assured we won’t be engaging with or working with ICE in any circumstances.”
McLaughlin stated, “ICE has taken action to ensure that detainees are not held for more than 12 hours, including by increasing staffing and other resources provided by the One Big Beautiful Bill. Secretary Noem has called on states and local government to assist with bed and detention space — but Portland has not answered that call for its nation.”
Sarah Bennett covers U.S. politics & news for content partner Modern Newsstand LLC.
